questions.problem: Find the exact solution of the equation ${3}^{x}=5.$
questions.worked_solution:
We take ${log}_{3}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{x} & =5 \\ {log}_{3}⁡({3}^{x}) & ={log}_{3}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x={log}_{3}⁡(5)
$$

questions.problem: Find the exact solution of the equation ${7}^{x+4}=5.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we take ${log}_{7}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{7}^{x+4} & =5 \\ {log}_{7}⁡({7}^{x+4}) & ={log}_{7}⁡(5)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that ${log}_{b}⁡({b}^{c})=c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+4={log}_{7}⁡(5)
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+4 & ={log}_{7}⁡(5) \\ x & ={log}_{7}⁡(5)-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x={log}_{7}⁡(5)-4.$

questions.problem: Given that ${11}^{4-y}=\sqrt[4]{3},$ find the value of $y$  rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Taking ${log}_{11}$ of both sides of the equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{11}^{4-y} & =\sqrt[4]{3} \\ {log}_{11}⁡({11}^{4-y}) & ={log}_{11}⁡(\sqrt[4]{3}) \\ 4-y & ={log}_{11}⁡({3}^{1/4})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power rule to the right-hand side:

$$
4-y=\frac{1}{4}{log}_{11}⁡(3)
$$

Next, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula and then solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4-y & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}{4\operatorname{log}⁡(11)} \\ -y & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}{4\operatorname{log}⁡(11)}-4 \\ y & =4-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}{4\operatorname{log}⁡(11)}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above on a calculator gives

$$
y≈3.885
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

questions.problem: Given that ${3}^{4-2x}=\sqrt{2},$ find the value of $x$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Taking ${log}_{3}$ of both sides of the equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{4-2x} & =\sqrt{2} \\ {log}_{3}⁡({3}^{4-2x}) & ={log}_{3}⁡(\sqrt{2}) \\ 4-2x & ={log}_{3}⁡({2}^{1/2})\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the power rule to the right-hand side:

$$
4-2x=\frac{1}{2}{log}_{3}⁡(2)
$$

Next, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula and then solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4-2x & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)}{2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)} \\ -2x & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)}{2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}-4 \\ x & =2-\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(2)}{4\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above on a calculator gives

$$
x≈1.842
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places

questions.problem: Find the exact solution to the equation $3({4}^{y})-14=19.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3({4}^{y})-14 & =19 \\ 3({4}^{y}) & =33 \\ {4}^{y} & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take ${log}_{4}$ of both sides of the equation and solve for $y$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{4}⁡({4}^{y}) & ={log}_{4}⁡(11) \\ y & ={log}_{4}⁡(11)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y={log}_{4}⁡(11).$

questions.problem: Given that ${5}^{2a+3}-13=25,$ find the value of $a$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation into a form that is more convenient for logarithms, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2a+3}-13 & =25 \\ {5}^{2a+3} & =38\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take ${log}_{5}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2a+3} & =38 \\ {log}_{5}⁡({5}^{2a+3}) & ={log}_{5}⁡(38) \\ 2a+3 & ={log}_{5}⁡(38)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}2a+3 & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(38)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)} \\ 2a & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(38)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)}-3 \\ a & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(38)}{2\operatorname{log}⁡(5)}-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above on a calculator gives

$$
a≈-0.370
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Example: 
                    Finding Exact Solutions to Exponential Equations Using Logarithms
canonical_examples.problem: Find the exact solution of the equation $2^{x+1}=3.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we take $\log_2$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{x+1} & =3 \\ {log}_{2}⁡({2}^{x+1}) & ={log}_{2}⁡(3)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\log_b \left( b^c \right) = c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
x+1 = \log_2 \left( 3 \right).
$$

Finally, we solve for $x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+1 & ={log}_{2}⁡(3) \\ x & ={log}_{2}⁡(3)-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x= \log_2 \left( 3 \right) - 1.$

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding Approximate Solutions to Exponential Equations Using Logarithms
canonical_examples.problem: Given that $3^{2x+3}=5,$ find the value of $x$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Taking $\log_3$ of both sides of the equation, we get

$$
\eqalign{
   	3^{2x+3} 				&= 5 \[3pt]
	\log_3 \left(3^{2x+3}\right)	&= \log_3 (5) \[3pt]
	2x+3 					&= \log_3 (5) . \[3pt]
}
$$

Then, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula and solve for $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+3 & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)} \\ 2x & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)}{\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}-3 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{log}⁡(5)}{2\operatorname{log}⁡(3)}-\frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating the above expression using a calculator gives

$$
x \approx -0.768
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

**Note:** We used the change of base formula to rewrite the right-hand side, as many calculators can only compute base $10$ logarithms.

canonical_examples.name:
Example: 
                    Finding Solutions to Exponential Equations when Rearrangement is Required
canonical_examples.problem: Given that $3\cdot 6^{x} = 9,$ find the value of $x$ rounded to $3$ decimal places.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the exponential on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\cdot {6}^{x} & =9 \\ {6}^{x} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we take $\log_{6}$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\eqalign{
   	6^x 					&= 3 \[3pt]
	\log_6 \left(6^x\right)	&= \log_6 (3) \[3pt]
	x 					&= \log_6 (3)\[3pt]
}
$$

Next, we rewrite the right-hand side using the change of base formula:

$$
x = \dfrac{\log(3)}{\log(6)}
$$

Evaluating the above on a calculator gives

$$
x \approx 0.613
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
We can use logarithms to solve equations where the variable is in an exponent.
For instance, suppose we are given the equation 

$$
{\color{blue}2}^x=5.
$$

Notice that the base of the exponential is ${\color{blue}2}.$ So, if we take $\log_{\color{blue}2}$ of both sides of the equation, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{2}⁡({2}^{x}) & ={log}_{2}⁡(5).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can use the fact that $\log_{\color{blue}b} \left( {\color{blue}b}^c \right) = c$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives

$$
x = \log_{\color{blue}2} (5).
$$

This is the solution! We often present the solution of an exponential equation as an exact solution in logarithmic form.

Note that when taking the $\log_b$ of both sides of an exponential equation, we always use the base of the exponential as the base of the logarithm.
